policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders 'the middle part of the city', which translates העיר (the ketiv), not חצר 'court'. The ASV note 'According to another reading, the middle court' explicitly relegates the qere חצר to an alternative reading, confirming the city reading is the one rendered in the text.
ASV reads 'shall they take away', a plural verb matching the qere יִקָּ֑חוּ; the ketiv יקח is singular ('shall he take') and is excluded by the English number.
